Samir — thanks for the clear list. Short answers here (we'll expand in the deck and during the session):

1) Data residency: in Hosted API the control plane metadata (routing, metrics) is in the hosted control plane; customer prompt/content data is encrypted in transit and at rest and may be processed in region-specific endpoints if requested (we can enable regional routing for EU/US/APAC). In Dedicated and Private deployments, all data stays in your VPC/cluster; Redwood control-plane reads are optional (we can run a private control plane). We'll add a slide showing exactly which components store which artifacts.

2) KV cache eviction: eviction is per-model worker process and per-conversation for active sessions; global cache eviction occurs only for memory pressure events. For very long chat context we support prefix compression and offloading to NVMe for less frequently accessed KV shards — we can demo latency tradeoffs in the session.

3) Throughput on short responses: on A100 we recommend batching targets of 16–32 requests for 12-token responses to maximize GPU utilization; latency P95 typically ~40–80ms depending on model size and sequence length. On T4, batching targets are smaller (8–16) with P95 ~80–140ms for similar workloads. We'll bring benchmark traces and a short script you can run in the sandbox.

Sandbox provisioning: we can provision a 7-day demo tenant. To get that ready I need the intended API usage (approx qps), the model family you want to test, and a contact for provisioning. Marcus attached a short provisioning how-to.

Proposed time tweak: we can move the meeting to 9:00 AM PT to accommodate APAC — Laura, can you update the invite?
